doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Listening to a recording and talk of his flutes
summary: Playback of But Beautiful, his octave switching, and the loss and cost of his best flutes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Can we listen to a little piece of something that I brought?
Oh I used to like that.

It does sound nice, doesn’t it? Boy, that holds up well I would say. Beautiful. In fact, the tune is “But Beautiful.” You know one thing I noticed about your playing is that you seem to really like to switch octaves frequently.

You know I don’t think I focused on that other than just naturally. I didn’t focus on the fact that I’m switching octaves. Also I guess a sad story I guess in that I’m still involved with it, is someone cut the head off that flute, it’s like a French flute, like cut off the head joint, and so it’s never been the same but there was supposed to be a good repairman and he didn’t ask me about doing it, and I didn’t know you could fit other heads in it, but I sold the flute and had some other flutes. You know you get rid of some good instruments that were good and then say why did I get rid of that? Because they got such a beautiful recorded sound and you don’t have it now. In fact I used another flute that has certain things but it doesn’t have some other things like I had a Powell that I recorded on Xanadu and some of the early days I recorded on a Haynes. Now I have a Haynes with another head and I can’t afford the beautiful — like one day James Galway came in with two gold flutes. He let me and my brother play his flutes. And what I mean is he had the $22,000 platinum or gold flutes. It’s beautiful how you can get a beautiful tone. But in

fact I heard it was stolen later on, I don’t know if he got them back or they sold his instruments, but what I mean a good instrument in the hands of a good player helps you play better. And I don’t have the access to the best instruments. But anyhow I like — the sound was so good because I had another instrument, plus my playing.
